epic.name: griot-r3f-starter
decisions: The controller must verify epic-hazine-hardening-delivery completed with a clean canonical repository, final public proof, and acceptance report before launching this epic.
Before launch, the controller must resolve or create the canonical starter repository and verify its baseline `pnpm run build` succeeds so the epic gate is safe after every story.
Use C:/Users/digit/GriotClients/griot-r3f-starter unless repository discovery resolves a different existing canonical home before creation.
TheDigitalGriot/r3f-vite-theatre-starter is reference input and is never silently overwritten.
All Hazine-specific names, values, brand assets, and licensed client models are removed or parameterized.
Generated dependency ranges are pinned and compatible.
risks: Client provenance leaking into a public sample
Starter behavior diverging from Hazine proofs

stories.title: Trace every exported primitive
stories.description: As a starter user, every exported primitive includes a provenance note naming the Hazine source module and acceptance check that proved it.

steps.description: Discover the canonical starter home without overwriting the reference repository.
Define a provenance record containing Hazine module, story/check, and parameterized/removed values.
Require one complete record for every public export.

context.why: Hazine remains the traceable proof source for generic primitives.
risks: Exports can be added without evidence.
edgeCases: One primitive combines several proven source modules.
patterns: Use the final Hazine public proof report evidence; no speculative exports.

stories.title: Configure reusable scene actors
stories.description: As a starter user, I can declare actors, visibility envelopes, transforms, responsive variants, preload groups, and material behavior in a typed scene manifest.

steps.description: Extract typed contracts from Hazine ActorDirector, profiles, manifest, and material lifecycle.
Parameterize all Hazine actor names, transforms, envelopes, and groups.
Verify array/glass lifecycle and responsive variants with neutral fixtures.

context.why: Scene behavior should be reusable without copying Hazine geometry assumptions.
risks: Overfitting types to Hazine's actor set.
edgeCases: Optional materials, empty groups, and envelope boundaries.
patterns: Extract only STORY-013, STORY-014, STORY-053, and STORY-054 proofs.

stories.title: Author reusable choreography
stories.description: As a starter user, I can configure normalized scroll chapters, camera keys, spline passages, Theatre synchronization, and reduced-motion behavior without Hazine-specific names or geometry.

steps.description: Extract normalized progress and named chapter contracts.
Generalize keyframe/spline and meaningful Theatre-property synchronization.
Provide deterministic reduced-motion resolution and neutral tests.

context.why: Authored spatial storytelling is the starter's core reusable capability.
edgeCases: Chapter boundary and spline endpoint behavior.
patterns: Use STORY-001 through STORY-004, STORY-008, and STORY-046 proofs.

stories.title: Bridge DOM and 3D state
stories.description: As a starter user, DOM controls, R3F reactions, data selection, and product-surface switching share a small predictable state bridge.

steps.description: Extract configurable progress, chapter, selection, surface, and playback slices.
Expose selectors/actions usable by DOM and R3F without frame-loop React writes.
Test same-frame selection and surface persistence with neutral data.

context.why: The product proof depends on one intelligence state across surfaces.
risks: A generic store can become an oversized framework.
edgeCases: Direct route initialization and component remounts.
patterns: Extract the minimum proven by STORY-021 through STORY-023 and STORY-031.

stories.title: Manage Anime.js lifecycle
stories.description: As a starter user, reusable Anime.js helpers scope animations to a root, replay safely, cancel on change/unmount, and honor live reduced-motion policy.

steps.description: Extract root-scoped target resolution and lifecycle cancellation.
Define replay semantics for rapid state changes.
Test unmount and live reduced-motion changes.

context.why: DOM motion must explain state without leaking or persisting incorrectly.
edgeCases: Rapid replay and preference change mid-animation.
patterns: Extract STORY-034, STORY-046, and STORY-047 behavior.

stories.title: Run a manifest-driven asset toolchain
stories.description: As a starter user, documented commands inspect, optionally repair, optimize, validate, promote, and generate gltfjsx output from a license-aware manifest.

steps.description: Extract and document the Hazine-proven manifest schema.
Parameterize every pipeline stage and license field.
Run twice from neutral source fixtures and compare outputs.

context.why: Reliable 3D projects need reproducible derivatives and attribution.
risks: Toolchain assumptions can be Windows- or Hazine-specific.

stories.title: Recover from scene failures
stories.description: As a starter user, reusable boundaries detect WebGL, report loading progress, contain scene/asset/module failures, offer retry, and preserve an authored static fallback.

steps.description: Extract classified loading/failure contracts and bounded retry.
Make fallback content configurable and DOM interaction-preserving.
Verify loading, broken asset, lazy failure, WebGL absence, and retry fixtures.

context.why: Resilience is part of the starter's quality floor.
risks: Fallback APIs can assume Hazine chapters.
patterns: Extract STORY-043 through STORY-045 and STORY-057.

stories.title: Configure responsive 3D profiles
stories.description: As a starter user, I can supply aspect-ratio-aware camera/actor profiles and verify them with standard viewport fixtures.

steps.description: Extract typed aspect-ratio profile selection.
Provide desktop/mobile and intermediate fixture definitions.
Verify resize/orientation behavior without Hazine coordinates.

context.why: Responsive spatial composition must be authored and testable.
risks: Only two hard-coded breakpoints do not generalize.

stories.title: Instrument adaptive scene performance
stories.description: As a starter user, I can opt into development performance instrumentation, adaptive DPR, lazy scene groups, bundle reports, and allocation-free render-loop examples.

steps.description: Extract lazy-group and no-allocation examples.
Add optional development metrics and adaptive DPR policy.
Generate bundle reports and verify production instrumentation is opt-in.

context.why: Teams need evidence-led performance controls without default fidelity loss.
risks: Adaptive DPR can oscillate or mask authoring problems.
edgeCases: Development panel excluded from production bundle.
patterns: Extract STORY-052, STORY-055, STORY-056, and STORY-063 proofs.

stories.title: Deploy beneath configurable base paths
stories.description: As a starter user, pinned compatible dependencies, configurable Vite base paths, SPA/subroute handling, and a GitHub Pages workflow deploy the sample beneath any repository subpath.

steps.description: Pin the Hazine-proven compatible dependency ranges.
Extract base-aware assets and root/subroute Pages fallback generation.
Run CI build/type/lint/test and public subpath deployment checks.

context.why: Deployment readiness must be built into the starter.
edgeCases: Trailing slash and direct nested-route refresh.
patterns: Extract STORY-005 through STORY-007 and STORY-064 through the final Hazine public proof.

stories.title: Ship a neutral documented sample
stories.description: As a starter user, I receive architecture and extension-point documentation, practical recipes, and a reduced Hazine-derived sample that contains no client brand assets or licensed models.

steps.description: Document architecture, extension points, dependency policy, and migration.
Add recipes for scroll stories, viewers, transitions, and dual DOM/3D surfaces.
Build a neutral reduced sample and scan output for Hazine brand/model files.
Compare fixtures against Hazine proofs and record exclusions/future tracks.

context.why: The starter must teach proven extension without leaking client identity.
risks: Example copy, filenames, or binary assets can retain client material.
patterns: Parameterize concepts; include no public/brand files or licensed GLBs.
